ai.title: CLI: Widen tool result type
ai.summary: Updated `ToolResultEvent` in `sdk-event-handlers.test.ts` to allow `any` values instead of strict strings. This resolves type conflicts in test mocks where tool outputs vary in structure. Scope limited to CLI test utilities.

eli5.text: The assistant's test code was being too strict about what kind of data it could handle, so the developers relaxed that rule. This mainly affects the people building and testing the assistant software itself, if you're just using the assistant, you wouldn't notice anything different. Behind the scenes, the testing files are now a bit more flexible, which should keep the software stable without changing how it works for you.

ai.title: Shared premium quota counter replaces per-model session usage
ai.summary: CLI model selector now displays a single shared premium quota count in the footer instead of per-model usage hints. Premium models share one quota pool, so the server replicates the same snapshot under each model id; the UI grabs the first entry to render the shared counter. MiniMax tagline drops 'unlimited' since it has no rateLimit payload. Changes affect cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx, status-bar.tsx, waiting-room-screen.tsx, and common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts.

eli5.text: You now see a single number in the status footer showing how many premium sessions you used out of the 5 available each rolling 20-hour window, regardless of which premium model you pick, replacing previous per-model usage lines. The list of premium models shows only a tier badge per row, and MiniMax models simply label themselves "Fastest" with no usage tracker, since they are unlimited. If you looked, you would no longer find per-model "X/Y used" hints on each row or separate quota lines in the waiting room screen. This is live today.

ai.title: Exclude TOOLCALLERROR from agent output
ai.summary: Tagged TOOL_CALL_ERROR messages are stripped from last_message and all_messages outputs in packages/agent-runtime/src/util/agent-output.ts. stream-parser.ts tags tool call errors with TOOL_CALL_ERROR. Filtering occurs after turn selection in getLastAssistantTurnMessages and getAgentOutput.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries to use a tool that doesn't exist or is used incorrectly, the error was previously shown to you in the response. Now those errors are hidden from your view, they still happen and get handled internally, but you won't see them mixed into the assistant's replies. This only applies to tool call failures, and it's live today.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.77 release bump in CLI package manifest
ai.summary: The `version` field in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` was updated from `0.0.76` to `0.0.77` as part of a release-bump commit. This packages the prior day's worth of user-facing changes, including the shared premium quota counter, CLI status bar cleanup, thinker output display fix, and TOOL_CALL_ERROR stripping from agent output. The change affects only the CLI release manifest used for binary distribution.
ai.evidence: Diff hunk in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` changes the `version` field from `0.0.76` to `0.0.77`; commit metadata is a release-bump with category Packaging.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.77 brings clearer output from AI agents and smarter tracking of your usage limits across premium AI models. The main changes include: agent results that previously disappeared now display correctly in your terminal, shared usage quotas that let you see how many premium sessions you have left across DeepSeek, Kimi, and GLM models in one place, and a cleaner status bar that no longer shows redundant labels. You also get cleaner error handling, since technical error messages from failed tool calls are now hidden from your view, and the model selector shows a single shared quota count instead of separate counts for each model. Upgrading means you'll see your AI results more reliably, understand your usage limits at a glance, and get a tidier interface when working with multiple premium AI models.

ai.title: DeepSeek image attachment handling
ai.summary: New `deepseek-request-body.ts` normalizes `ChatCompletionRequestBody` to strip unsupported `image_url` and `file` parts, replacing them with text notices. `types.ts` updates `ChatMessage.content` to accept `ChatCompletionContentPart[]`. Refactors `deepseek.ts` to use shared model IDs and request builders.

eli5.text: When you chat with the DeepSeek model through this system, any images or files you attach will now be quietly replaced with a short text note saying they were left out, rather than causing the request to fail. The system also now correctly translates the model's 'thinking' responses instead of mislabeling them, and bills you based on a single shared price list for all DeepSeek models. If you look at the chat, you won't see broken image placeholders or confusing pricing errors anymore.

ai.title: browser-use agent enabled in free mode
ai.summary: The `browser-use` agent is added to `FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS` in `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts`, mapped to `google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview`. This enables browser automation capabilities for free-tier users. The change applies to the shared core constants, affecting all surfaces (Web, CLI, Desktop) that consume this configuration.

eli5.text: If you use the free version, the assistant can now control a web browser for you, opening pages, clicking around, and reading what shows up, all automatically instead of you guiding it yourself. This browser automation ability was added to the list of tools that the free tier is allowed to use, backed by the same lightweight model it already uses. The change went live on 2026-05-05 and applies wherever free accounts get their settings, so right now it covers the website, the command-line tool, and the desktop app.

ai.title: Remove stale AGENTS.md docs reference
ai.summary: Deleted the `docs/patterns/discover-before-implement.md` line from AGENTS.md. The file was missing from the repo, making the reference dead. Scope is limited to AGENTS.md.

eli5.text: A reference to a missing documentation page was removed from the AGENTS.md file, which lists helpful guides for developers. The linked file had already been deleted from the repository, so the entry was simply pointing to nothing. This only affects the AGENTS.md listing and nothing else, leaving all other references intact. The change is in place today.

ai.title: CLI takeover prompt for concurrent Freebuff instances
ai.summary: Added a local-only `takeover_prompt` session status to the CLI. When a second instance starts while another is already running, the new instance prompts the user to either take over the session or exit. This prevents accidental session rotation or conflicts without requiring a server-side change.

eli5.text: If you open the command-line helper while it is already running for your account, the new one will now stop and ask you whether you want to take over the session or quit, instead of silently replacing the first one. The choice appears in your terminal before any data is sent to the server, so no work is interrupted unless you confirm. This is live today and only affects people running the command-line version locally; the web interface is unchanged.

ai.title: Deterministic tool call ids replace random UUIDs in Agent Runtime
ai.summary: Agent Runtime now generates deterministic tool call ids formatted as `functions.<toolName>:<index>` via `createToolCallIdGenerator`, replacing random `crypto.randomUUID` and `generateCompactId` calls. This change ensures stable ids for tool calls across retries or re-parses by counting existing tool calls in message history and pending calls. Affected files include `run-programmatic-step.ts`, `tool-stream-parser.ts`, `tools/stream-parser.ts`, and `tools/tool-executor.ts` within `packages/agent-runtime`. The new `util/tool-call-id.ts` module handles id generation and counting logic.

eli5.text: When the assistant asks itself to use a tool (like a calculator or a web search) during a conversation, it now gives that tool call a predictable, traceable label instead of a random one. This means if the same request happens again or gets replayed, the assistant can reliably match the tool it called with the answer it got back, making retries and re-parsing smoother. You wouldn't see this directly, but you'd notice fewer mix-ups when the assistant repeats or revisits a step that involved using a tool. The change is live today for everyone using the agent runtime.

ai.title: Improve codesearch output formatting
ai.summary: Code search output now groups matches by file with explicit line numbers and includes a global match count header. The formatting logic in common/src/util/format-code-search.ts was refactored to parse ripgrep lines more robustly, handling both match and context lines. In sdk/src/tools/code-search.ts, the output truncation now applies to the formatted string rather than raw stdout, ensuring the match count header and grouping structure are preserved even when output is limited.

eli5.text: When the assistant searches your codebase, the results now open with a count of how many matches were found, and matches are listed grouped by file with clear line numbers. You will see a line like "Found 3 matches" at the top, followed by each file's name, then its matching lines indented and numbered. If the results would be very long, the assistant now truncates the final readable text rather than the raw stream, so the summary header and file grouping stay intact instead of being cut off.

ai.title: Rename str replace replacement fields to old String and new String
ai.summary: The str_replace and propose_str_replace tool parameter schemas were updated so the replacement objects use `oldString` and `newString` instead of the short `old` and `new` keys. The change spans the type declarations in `.agents/types/tools.ts`, `agents/types/tools.ts`, and `common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types/tools.ts`, the zod schemas in `common/src/tools/params/tool/str-replace.ts` and `common/src/tools/params/tool/propose-str-replace.ts`, the alias normalization in `common/src/tools/params/utils.ts`, the runtime destructure in `packages/agent-runtime/src/process-str-replace.ts`, the validation hints in `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts`, the SDK result messages in `sdk/src/tools/change-file.ts`, and the agent instruction prompts baked into `agents-graveyard/editor/reviewer-editor.ts`, `agents/editor/best-of-n/editor-implementor.ts`, and `agents/editor/editor.ts`. The CLI rendering side was simplified in `cli/src/components/tools/str-replace.tsx`, which drops its inline `extractValueForKey` parser and instead delegates to the shared `extractDiff`, `extractFilePath`, and `isCreateFile` helpers imported from `../../utils/implementor-helpers`, so the component now guards the diff viewer with `diffText.length > 0`.
ai.evidence: The diff renames the `old`/`new` replacement fields to `oldString`/`newString` in the `StrReplaceParams` and `ProposeStrReplaceParams` schemas within `.agents/types/tools.ts`, `agents/types/tools.ts`, and `common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types/tools.ts`; updates agent instruction prompts in `agents-graveyard/editor/reviewer-editor.ts`, `agents/editor/best-of-n/editor-implementor.ts`, and `agents/editor/editor.ts` to reference `oldString`/`newString`; and rewrites `cli/src/components/tools/str-replace.tsx` to remove its local `extractValueForKey` parser and instead call `extractDiff`, `extractFilePath`, and `isCreateFile` from `../../utils/implementor-helpers`.
ai.migration: If you use the str_replace or propose_str_replace tool, update any integration that reads or emits the old `old`/`new` keys to use `oldString`/`newString` instead.

changes.what: Renamed the str_replace and propose_str_replace replacement fields from `old`/`new` to `oldString`/`newString`.
Updated the zod schemas and alias normalization so the replacement objects use `oldString`/`newString`.
Destructured the replacement objects as `oldString`/`newString` in the str_replace processor.
Adjusted the change-file tool to produce the new success and failure result messages.
Removed the local diff parser in str-replace.tsx and reused the shared implementor-helpers extractors.
Updated editor agent instruction prompts and examples to use the new field names.

ai.title: Add keyboard navigation to CLI waiting room
ai.summary: Keyboard navigation replaces mouse-only interaction in `cli/src/components/waiting-room-screen.tsx`. Arrow keys and Tab cycle focus between 'Take over' and 'Exit' buttons, with Enter activating the focused option. Visual borders highlight the active button.

eli5.text: When the command-line tool detects that another copy is already running, it shows a screen with two options: 'Take over' (end the other instance and use this one) or 'Exit' (quit and keep using the existing one). You can now use the left and right arrow keys, the Tab key, or Shift+Tab to move a highlighted border between those two buttons, and press Enter to confirm the one that's highlighted. Before this, the cursor keys and Tab did nothing, and you had to know the keyboard shortcut (Enter for take over, Escape for exit) without any on-screen cue about which action was active. The screen is live now, so anyone starting a second instance will see the border appear around a button as they navigate with the keyboard.

ai.title: Freebuff premium sessions reset at Pacific midnight
ai.summary: Premium session quota counting shifted from rolling 20-hour window to daily Pacific midnight reset. Server counts `free_session_admit` rows since last midnight `America/Los_Angeles`; limit remains 5 sessions. CLI waiting-room UI, `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, and `web/src/server/free-session/public-api.ts` updated. `FREEBUFF_PREMIUM_SESSION_WINDOW_HOURS` constant deprecated, replaced by `FREEBUFF_PREMIUM_SESSION_RESET_TIMEZONE` and `FREEBUFF_PREMIUM_SESSION_PERIOD`.

ai.title: Fix freebuff model tab navigation
ai.summary: Refactored key event handling in `freebuff-model-selector.tsx` to use new `freebuffModelNavigationDirectionForKey` utility. Added explicit support for raw ANSI escape sequences for Tab and Shift+Tab navigation in `freebuff-model-navigation.ts`. Applied `stopPropagation` to prevent conflicting key handling.

eli5.text: When you open the list of AI models you can pick in the CLI tool, pressing Tab and Shift+Tab now reliably moves your selection forward and backward through the models. Previously, depending on your terminal, those keys could be missed or handled inconsistently, so sometimes nothing would move. The keyboard handling was reworked to translate key presses into a clear forward/backward direction and stop the keys from triggering anything else at the same time. This is live today for anyone using the model selector in the CLI.
